newsitem.title: PAKISTAN: Pakistani bourse wants lower phone call rates.
newsitem.headline: Pakistani bourse wants lower phone call rates.

text.p: Pakistan's main Karachi Stock Exchange (KSE) urged the government on Saturday to drop excise duty on local and international telephone calls.

The KSE said in a statement it had made the proposal for inclusion in the next national budget for fiscal 1997/98 (July/June) to raise the profitability of the state-run Pakistan Telecommunication Company Ltd (PTCL) and help the stock market.
"We would urge that the government should consider waiving the excise duty (on telephone calls) and letting the differential remain with the PTCL to improve its profit margins," it said.

In August 1994, the government disinvested three percent of PTCL equity to the general public at 30 rupees per share and later made an international offering of nine percent that fetched 55 rupees per share, the KSE said.

"The fate of the foreign investors in the PTCL equity must be extremely disheartening to those who may be contemplating either to make portfolio investments in our equity market or to participate in privatisation," the statement said.
On Friday, Communications Minister Azam Khan Hoti said in a speech the government had put off the planned privatisation of the telecommunication sector until it could get a better price.
The KSE said the government had suffered a loss of 132 billion rupees as the PTCL stock value had gradually fallen to 25.35 rupees on Friday from 55 in 1994.

"This is a staggering loss and great attention must be paid to improving the PTCL profitability," the KSE statement KSE said, adding, "For the stock market, PTCL represents a third of the market capitalisation and a third of trading volume."
